fields.AN_Notes: Qualitative interview study (reflexive thematic analysis) with 19 users of generative AI chatbots (mainly Pi and ChatGPT) for mental health; themes emotional sanctuary, insightful guidance, joy of connection, AI therapist. Soziale_Arbeit coded ja as interpretation: the work centres psychosocial support and counselling for people with mental health problems, a target group and practice field of social work (Mental_Health), although social work is not named. Inequality appears only as unequal reach: the well-educated, tech-savvy sample suggests the benefits may not reach the full population in need; coded Exclusionary_Norms (assumption of digitally skilled users) with the proposed digital-navigator role as organisational remedy. Digital skill is no social axis under the codebook, so AN_Bias_Axes None; bias in the sense of discrimination is no object, hence AN_Bias_Definition Not_Applicable. Prompting is not treated; participants' role-play requests are described usage only. Inductive analysis without theory frame.

Bias axes from the work's own worked examples: Black women in image recognition (gender, race, intersectional) and the Dutch childcare benefits and French welfare fraud cases (dual nationality, immigrant background). Harm: unequal error rates for darker-skinned women used as worked example (Disparate_Performance); the welfare cases are allocational but the work does not classify them as direct or indirect discrimination, so no discrimination value is coded. Mitigation: organisational and participatory recommendations, Proposed; the expert workshop assessed perceived actionability and barriers of the recommendations, not their effect on bias, so the status is not raised to Evaluated. Soziale_Arbeit teilweise through welfare-administration cases as motivation; AN_Population Not_SW_Specific because the addressees are AI experts. Gender is not defined; race is explicitly called a social construct, gender is treated through systemic sexism and intersectionality. Theories: intersectionality after Collins and Bilge and Crenshaw, Young's structural definition of injustice, Kong's weak versus strong fairness.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual article on the presence/mediation and technique/critique tensions of algorithmic decision-making in social work, worked through case studies (AFST, COMPAS, NDIS, HEALER, Heat List) and a proposal for a practice-embedded critical-technical pedagogy. Bias axes from the case studies: race (COMPAS error rates, over-policing of African-American communities through Heat List) and disability (practitioner bias toward children with disability, NDIS scores overlooking the impact of disability); misogyny and heterosexism appear only in an enumeration, so gender is no object. Harms: unequal false-negative rates (Disparate_Performance) and risk scores from invalid correlations and assumed group characteristics or network proximity (Indirect_Discrimination). Mitigation: organisational and educational measures (mandatory human screening of high scores, algorithmic literacy, case-study pedagogy); Demonstrated because the authors use the case-study method in their own teaching and report student reasoning, without an assessment. Theory: critical theories of social power and technology, sociology of science and technology, critical race theory in the pedagogy; borderline because they frame the curriculum more than a definition of bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Invited commentary on opportunities and ethical challenges of ChatGPT for social work science, with five recommendations (transparency, fact-checking, authorship, attribution, inclusion and social justice). General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'develop prompts that explicitly ask to identify the work of BIPOC scholars and resources and perspectives from underrepresented communities'; transparency also asks to document how the LLM was used with prompts. Bias axes: race (BIPOC, white-centric content) and language/cultural region (mainstream white English, Eurocentric content, Global South); gender, sexuality, ability and caste appear only in an enumeration and are not coded, so gender is no object (Not_Applicable). Harms argued for the work's own object: exclusion of BIPOC and Global South literature (Erasure) and white-centric/Eurocentric defaults (Exclusionary_Norms). Mitigation proposed: inclusive prompting and an ethical framework from professional bodies. Tasks: research (questions, qualitative themes, transcripts, manuscripts) and teaching (academic misconduct, assessment of student papers). Theory reference: an antiracist research framework (Goings et al. 2023) and the bureaucratic-algorithm argument of Caplan and Boyd frame the treatment of bias, borderline because both are invoked briefly.

fields.AN_Notes: Survey with a taxonomy of intersectional fairness notions (subgroup, calibration-based, metric-based, differential, max-min, probabilistic fairness) and fair-learning methods with and without demographics, plus NLP, ranking and auditing applications. Gender and race are the worked axes through the Black-woman example; other attributes appear only in dataset tables or cited studies. Harm types: subgroup accuracy and worst-case loss disparities (Disparate_Performance) and the 80-percent disparate-impact rule extended to intersectional groups (Indirect_Discrimination); the other outcome-parity notions are not classified as direct or indirect by the work. Mitigation stages each with synthesised support: dataset coverage (Pre_Processing), auditing/adversarial reweighting during learning (In_Training), multicalibration and multiaccuracy post-processing (Post_Processing), stakeholder involvement (Organisational_Process, proposed only). Evaluated refers to synthesised evaluations, e.g. Subramanian et al. 2021 evaluating two debiasing techniques with the result that independent-group debiasing is prone to gerrymandering, and Lahoti et al. 2020 reporting improved fairness for some intersectional groups; the survey runs no own experiment. Gender appears as a categorical protected attribute (male/female, Black female) without definition. Feministisch teilweise: intersectionality is adopted as a formal fairness concept, power analysis is limited to the gerrymandering critique.

fields.AN_Notes: German practice guide for managers and staff in small and medium enterprises with the KI-FAIRNESS framework (Kontext, Input, Fokus, Ausschnitt, Iterationen, Repertoire, Nachbessern, Eignung, Sprache, Sinn). General_Guidance strategies verbatim: 'Am besten ist es daher, Prompts auf Englisch zu formulieren und in die Beschreibung explizit die gewünschte Darstellung von weiblichen und männlichen Chef*innen aufzunehmen'; gender-neutral prompts for recommendation letters and a 'Verwirrungstaktik' naming both genders; explicitly requesting women and men, different skin colours and social classes instead of adding 'divers'. ICL: uploading examples of the desired style; Role_Persona: prompt element 'Rolle'. Bias axes from the guide's own DALL-E 2 and Midjourney trials (gender, skin colour, age, slimness, no persons with disability, privileged settings); Women of Color sexualisation is a cited news example, so Intersectional is not coded. Hiring discrimination appears only as a hypothetical example and stays uncoded. Mitigation_Status Demonstrated: the guide applies prompt variants and reports informal observations (adding 'divers' changed little) without a systematic assessment. Organisational measures (strategy, governance, diverse teams, training, four-eyes review), representative data and targeted training are recommendations. AN_Task Other_Task: drafting job advertisements, recommendation letters and marketing images in companies. Gender analysis follows women and men, genderqueer people are mentioned once in the gender data gap. Theory reference is weak: the gender data gap concept and the feminist AI narrative frame the treatment of bias. Publication type borderline: practice guide from a university of applied sciences, treated as scholarly grey literature.
